transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 09:30 PST | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Daniel (Lucent - Head of Search), Priya (Lucent - ML Eng), Oliver (CTO - joined 10m in)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed lucent current stack (elastic + custom scaler), embedding models, vector DBs, throughput targets, privacy/security requirements; next steps = benchmark, pricing, security docs.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood Inference, with Ethan our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:08] Daniel: Daniel here, head of search at Lucent, we own internal search and support search, been reworking relevance - currently elastic + custom signals.
[00:14] Priya: Priya, ML eng, i've been looking at embeddings pipelines and rerank models.
[00:18] Ethan: Great, hi all. Oliver?
[00:20] Oliver: Hey, sorry for joining a bit late, CTO.
[00:23] Maya: Cool. Today we want to understand your retrieval stack, metrics for success, and show how redwood can fit into hosted, dedicated, or private deployments for embeddings + reranking.

[02:10] Daniel: High level — we serve a product+support search for SaaS customers, mostly enterprise. Traffic pattern: steady baseline ~200 qps, spikes up to ~2k qps during incidents. Latency SLOs are tight — p95 < 200ms for first-pass retrieval and ideally end-to-end < 500ms after rerank. Cost is a big consideration.

[03:05] Priya: We today compute 768-dim embeddings offline with a custom bi-encoder, store in Elastic as dense_vectors right now, and we do BM25 first pass then embedding rerank top 100. We're evaluating switching to vector DB - looking at Pinecone and Milvus.

[03:40] Ethan: Got it. Typical hybrid. Couple questions: what's your average doc size and index cardinality? and are you ok with approximate search (ANN) for recall vs exact?

[03:48] Priya: Index size ~12M docs, avg doc length 600 tokens. We currently rerank with a cross-encoder on the top 100 results; reranker adds ~120ms on average. We try to keep topk small to constrain cost.

[04:20] Daniel: Our QA team cares about recall — false negatives are visible in support routing. So we can't sacrifice recall too much. But we also need consistent latency, so tradeoffs are annoying.

[05:00] Maya: On the Redwood side, we support hosted API for rapid start, dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput, and private VPC/on-prem for enterprise. For embeddings you can use our managed embedding models or bring-your-own. We integrate with vector DBs or you can use Redwood to store embeddings and do nearest-neighbor in our runtime.

[05:30] Daniel: Storing in Redwood runtime — is that stateful? how does persistence and scaling look?

[05:38] Ethan: Good question. When customers want low-latency high-throughput we recommend Dedicated with local shard placement + KV caching; for persistence we're compatible with S3/backing store for checkpoints and our runtime keeps an in-memory/quantized index for hot shards. Alternatively, Redwood can act purely as the embedding/querier and push vectors to your DB like Pinecone or Milvus.

[06:10] Priya: We want to avoid forklift changes; ideally Redwood can plug into our existing Milvus or Pinecone and handle embedding generation + rerank. Also curious about dimensionality: we may move from 768->512 for speed — any guidance?

[06:28] Ethan: 512 dims gives ~30% lower memory and faster sim compute, generally fine if model fidelity is preserved. If you quantize, 8-bit/4-bit can further cut memory. Our optimizer provides recommended dims and quantization per target recall/latency. We'll run a probe.

[07:05] Daniel: For ANN, we were thinking HNSW on Milvus, would Redwood accept vector stores with HNSW and provide cross-encoder rerank?

[07:15] Ethan: Absolutely. Typical pattern: BM25 -> ANN top-k (100) -> cross-encoder rerank in Redwood. We're also able to do lightweight rerank models in the runtime to reduce cost. We have connectors to Milvus/Pinecone and can stream query vectors -> DB -> gather IDs -> fetch documents -> run rerank.

[08:02] Oliver: Security: we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS for keys, and audit logs. Also data residency for EU customers.

[08:15] Maya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, supports SAML SSO, KMS integrations, and dedicated private deploys for EU. We'll share the security pack after call.

[08:32] Daniel: Great. On throughput, can dedicated pools sustain 2k qps with rerank? what GPU types?

[08:45] Ethan: It depends on reranker size and whether you batch. For a cross-encoder like a small L2 (eg, 6-12 layers) on A100-equivalent, you can get ~100-300 qps per GPU for rerank depending on sequence length; with dedicated pools and sharding you can scale horizontally. If reranker is big, we recommend batching and autoscaling. For strict latency SLOs we use hot shards + local caching and burst capacity. We'll test with your exact model and sequence lengths.

[09:30] Priya: What about cost comparison between doing everything in Redwood vs using our existing Milvus and only using Redwood for embeddings+rerank?

[09:40] Maya: Typical pattern: using Redwood for embedding generation and rerank, keeping ANN in your DB, tends to be cost-effective because vector search is cheaper on purpose-built vector stores. If you move index into Redwood runtime to avoid network hop, cost goes up but latency improves. We can model cost in the benchmark.

[10:20] Daniel: We saw Redwood benchmarks but want to run on our data. Can we have a script and sample harness?

[10:25] Ethan: Yes, we'll provide a harness. We'll need sample dataset, query sets, and target metrics (recall@k, latency p95, cost estimate). We have a shared spreadsheet template — bit.ly/lucent-rerank for results tracking.

[11:05] Priya: Our query mix has a heavy long-tail of support queries and shorter product browse queries. We'll provide a representative 2k query sample for the benchmark.

[11:15] Ethan: Perfect. For the benchmark we'll propose: 768-dim and 512-dim runs, ANN top-100, cross-encoder rerank on top-100, measure p50/p95 latency and throughput sustained to 2k qps (or scaled run). We'll run hosted pilot first (small scale) then dedicated pilot for realistic throughput.

[12:00] Daniel: What about replica consistency and idempotency? We have frequent index updates during release windows.

[12:08] Ethan: We support index snapshotting and rolling updates; for dedicated we can orchestrate draining shards and warm new ones. For online updates you can stream embeddings; we also support TTL and partial refresh. We'll include notes in the playbook.

[12:30] Maya: Quick question on integration surface: what SDKs do you provide and how is auth handled?

[12:36] Ethan: We provide REST and Python SDKs. Auth via API keys for hosted, and SAML/OAuth for private. For dedicated you get tenant-level keys and can integrate with your KMS.

[13:05] Oliver: Any limits on embedding dimensionality or payload per vector? Also does Redwood store metadata with vectors and how's that exposed?

[13:13] Ethan: No hard limit on dim, but memory and cost scale linearly. Metadata is supported as opaque fields that we pass through; if you use our runtime index we store lightweight pointers and you can fetch full docs from your store.

[14:00] Daniel: Are there common gotchas around BM25 + embed hybrid ranking? sometimes BM25 outranks embeddings for short queries.

[14:08] Priya: yes we tuned weights but it's brittle. We'd like Redwood guidance on hybrid scoring and telemetry.

[14:16] Ethan: We provide telemetry per route and per model, plus token-level cost and latency breakdowns in console. We can instrument hybrid score weights and run A/B tests. Also can do canary rollouts by user segment.

[15:05] Daniel: Ok sounds good. Any compliance for on-prem?

[15:12] Maya: For regulated workloads we offer private deployments and an on-prem bundle. We can discuss packaging and enterprise licensing after initial benchmark.

[15:45] Priya: For the reranker, we might start with a distilled cross-encoder to hit latency. Do you support switching models in flight?

[15:54] Ethan: Yes, our rollout system supports model version pinning, A/B and canary and automatic fallback to cheaper variants.

[16:20] Daniel: What about caching prefix/KV? can that help with spikes?

[16:25] Ethan: We have automatic prefix caching for repeated prefixes and KV cache for hot document embeddings. Works well for incident spikes where queries repeat.

[17:00] Maya: Next steps recap — we'll send pricing and security docs; Ethan will share the benchmark harness and schedule the pilot; Priya to share dataset and query set; follow-up to review results week of Mar 16.

[17:30] Daniel: That works. Any final questions?
[17:35] Oliver: No, just want the security pack.

[17:40] Maya: We'll send it after. Thanks all.

[17:50] (call ends)

Notes/Artifacts referenced: shared benchmark spreadsheet: bit.ly/lucent-rerank; security pack link (will be sent); pricing proposal (to be shared).
